extra.message: The unauthenticated `username` query parameter is interpolated into an SQL f-string and passed through `run_sql_query()` to `db.execute()` without parameter binding. An attacker can inject SQL through `/select?username=...`.

All attacker-controlled fields of the `User` request body are interpolated into the INSERT SQL f-string, which is executed by `run_sql_query()` without parameterization. Quotes or SQL syntax in any field can alter the query.
The `username` query parameter is interpolated directly into a DELETE SQL statement and executed without parameter binding, allowing SQL injection through `DELETE /user`.
The attacker-controlled `user.address` value is interpolated directly into a DELETE SQL statement without quoting or parameter binding. Crafted SQL tokens can alter the deletion predicate.

`POST /find` accepts arbitrary JSON and passes it unchanged to `users.find(query)`. An attacker can supply database query operators, such as `$in`, to control the NoSQL query and retrieve records beyond an intended username lookup.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in NoSQL Query

extra.message: `GET /select` exposes user records with no authentication or authorization dependency. The same application contains no authentication middleware, and `/find` endpoints similarly expose records to anonymous callers.

extra.message: `POST /reset` deletes both database stores and recreates them without any authentication or authorization check. Any remote caller can erase all application data.
